chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu al-Khazraj al-Hasan ibn al-Zibrqan al-Ansari, who said: Is'haq al-Hadda' told me, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) sent for me while we were in Mina: 'Come to me, and with you are your tools.' So I went to him in his tent, greeted him, and he responded and gestured for me to sit. So I sat down. Then he took a new sandal and threw it to me. When I wanted to leave, I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! If you were to gift me this sandal, I could replicate it.' So he threw the other one to me and said, 'One? What benefit can it give you?' He said, 'And it was such that it has a support for the heel, narrow from its middle, and for it were two straps, and for it were heads. So he said: This is the footwear of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).'.

key_terms.قِبَالَانِ: Two straps (typically across the top of the foot)
key_terms.كِنْفُكَ: Your tools or equipment (referring to the companion's trade)
key_terms.مُعَقَّبَةً: Having a heel support or strap that goes around the heel
key_terms.مِنْى: Mina, a location near Mecca where pilgrims stay during Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the sandal gifted by Imam al-Sadiq in this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the concept of *tawathur* (consecutive transmission) in Shia scholarship, where material artifacts serve as tangible proofs of prophetic tradition (*Sunnah*). The Imam’s specific identification of the sandal’s design—described as *mu'abbah* (tied) and *mukhassarah* (shortened)—emphasizes the preservation of the Prophet’s physical appearance and customs (*sunan*) through direct lineage, reinforcing the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt in interpreting religious practice.
